name: mazda_13b_fc_na
label: Mazda 13B 1.3 L two-rotor (RX-7 FC, peripheral exhaust port)
based_on: Mazda 13B six-port, naturally aspirated (RX-7 FC Series 5, 1989-1991)

sources.what: Mazda 1989 RX-7 workshop manual, Technical Data section (scan): compression ratio, port timing, idle speed, throttle throat diameters, rotor housing width.
SAE paper 2004-01-1790 (Mazda): 13B-family rotor geometry (15 x 105 x 80 mm), peripheral exhaust port, and a cross-check of the intake opening at 32 degrees after top dead centre.
supercars.net specification page for the 1989 RX-7 GTUs: power, torque and redline. An enthusiast site, not a Mazda document.
Wikipedia, Mazda RX-7: Series 5 naturally aspirated engine, 160 hp, 9.7:1.

notes: Sourced: compression ratio, port timing, idle speed, throttle throats, rotor width (1989 factory manual); eccentricity and rotor radius are the 13B family's from Mazda's SAE paper, not stated in the FC manual itself; power, torque and the 8000 rpm redline come from an enthusiast specification page, not a Mazda document. Port timing is the manual's table converted to shaft degrees after a chamber's firing top dead centre: exhaust opens 75 before bottom centre (270 - 75 = 195) and closes 48 after top centre (540 + 48 = 588); the intake window runs from the primary and secondary ports opening 32 after top centre (540 + 32 = 572) to the auxiliary port closing 80 after bottom centre (810 + 80 = 890). Overlap is 16 degrees. The exhaust duration of 393 degrees fits a peripheral port about 11 degrees wide on the housing. Not expressible here: the real engine has three intake ports per rotor (primary 32 to 40, secondary 32 to 30, auxiliary 45 to 80), with the auxiliary ports opened by valves at higher speed (the speed was not found); this definition has one window with all ports open at every speed. The throttle is one bore of the same area as the manual's three 45 mm throats (77.9 mm, a calculation). Assumed, not sourced: the two rotors 180 degrees apart. Estimated, not sourced: port flow areas, intake runner length and diameter, plenum and airbox sizes (derived defaults), every exhaust dimension, flywheel inertia, burn duration scale and the heat release value (tuned, with runner length and port areas, toward the published output).

vehicle.name: Mazda RX-7 GTUs (FC, US, 1989)
vehicle.notes: The GTUs was chosen because the engine research's output figures come from the same supercars.net GTUs page; it is the sportier naturally aspirated FC (4.30 limited-slip differential, 16-inch wheels). No Mazda document, manual or period road test was reachable: every value is from an enthusiast spec site, and an owners'-club table disagrees on the GTUs gear ratios (3.67 / 2.22 / 1.43 / 1.00 / 0.76) and weight (2725 lb). The site's top speed (about 130 mph) is marked as an estimate and is omitted. wheel_radius_m is my calculation from the tyre size (half the rim diameter plus section width times aspect ratio): the unloaded radius; the loaded rolling radius is a few percent smaller.
